xref.title: Birthplace and Early Life (1980)
xref.body: Win Butler, whose real name is Edwin, is the singer for Arcade Fire. He was born in Truckee, California, a remote location in the northeast corner of the state on the border with Nevada, before his family relocated to The Woodlands, a planned community north of Houston, Texas. "He was born into a place called Truckee, California."

xref.title: Edwin Left 1997 Solo; Brian Byrne Tape Initially Thrown Out, Then Hired; Edwin Returned 2016
xref.body: I Mother Earth formed when Jagori Tanna and Christian Tanna met Edwin at their shared rehearsal space in 1990, creating a band immediately subject to a major-label bidding war. Edwin left in 1997 to go solo, finishing tour commitments that summer. The following year, auditions began; hundreds of demo tapes arrived, including one from a Newfoundlander named Brian Byrne that was immediately discarded. A mutual friend insisted they look again; Brian got a second chance, got the gig, and served as singer from 1998 to 2003. After a long hiatus, a 2012 reunion brought Brian back; Edwin was invited back again in 2016. Both occasionally share the stage on current tours. "His tape was immediately thrown out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Brain Surgery and Post-Stroke Speech (2005)
xref.body: Less than a week after his hemorrhages, Edwin underwent brain surgery to relieve pressure in his skull. For weeks afterward, he could only utter four phrases: "Yes," "No," "Grace Maxwell" (his wife's name), and "The possibilities are endless." "for weeks afterwards, he could only say four things. Yes, no. Grace Maxwell, which is the name of his wife, and weirdly, the possibilities are endless."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Cerebral Hemorrhages (February 18, 2005)
xref.body: On February 18, 2005, during a BBC visit, Edwin Collins felt unwell, experiencing dizziness and nausea. Two days later, he was in intensive care after suffering a major cerebral hemorrhage, described by doctors as "catastrophic." He then suffered a second, equally catastrophic hemorrhage. "Two days later though, he was an intensive care having suffered a major cerebral hemorrhage, bad bleeding of the brain. And then another one. And both were described as catastrophic."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Edwin Forms Crash Karma (2008)
xref.body: In 2008, Edwin partnered with Mike Turner (formerly of Our Lady Peace) and Jeff Burrows (of The Tea Party) to form the band Crash Karma. "Then in 2008, he joined up with Mike Turner, ex of our lady piece, and Jeff Burrows of the Tea Party in a band called Crash Karma."

xref.title: Cerebral Hemorrhages and Stroke
xref.body: On February 18, 2005, Edwin Collins experienced a series of major cerebral hemorrhages, or catastrophic brain bleeding, shortly after feeling unwell during a BBC interview. Within two days, he was in intensive care, and less than a week later, he underwent surgery to alleviate pressure on his skull. "Edwin had suffered a major cerebral hemorrhage, and then another one. And then another one. Catastrophic bleeding of the brain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Christian Samson's Post-Band Career
xref.body: Drummer Christian Samson played with Edwin after his departure from I Mother Earth, had brief stints with Moist and the prog rock group Saga, and now manages his own HVAC condo service. This shows a diverse career path both within and outside the music industry. "drummer Christian Samson played around with Edwin after he left I Mother Earth. There was also a short stint in Moist and with saga, the Prague Rock Group, and he's now running his own HVAC condo service."

xref.title: Continued Music Career Post-Stroke
xref.body: Four years after his stroke, Edwin Collins resumed recording music. Although his right hand's impairment prevents him from strumming a guitar, he retains the ability to form chords. While he now walks with a cane and speaks with a stutter, his singing voice remains unaffected, and he continues to release records. "He does stutter when he speaks, but when he sings, there's no trouble at all. Four years after the stroke, he started recording music again."

xref.title: Falling and Laughing, the Restoration of Edwin Collins (Book)
xref.body: This inspiring book chronicles Edwin Collins' journey to recovery from his brain aneurysm and stroke, authored by his wife, Grace Maxwell, who was instrumental in his rehabilitation. "If you're ever looking to read an inspiring book, his wife Grace is the author of Falling and Laughing, the Restoration of Edwin Collins."

xref.title: Limited Post-Stroke Communication
xref.body: Following his severe strokes, Edwin Collins' ability to speak was significantly impaired for weeks, during which he could only utter four distinct phrases: "yes," "no," the name of his wife, Grace Maxwell, and "the possibilities are endless." "For weeks afterwards, he could only say four things. Yes, no. The name of his wife, Grace Maxwell. And for reasons that no one can explain, the possibilities are endless."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mellower Disposition and Bird Watching
xref.body: Edwin Collins reports that his experiences have made him a much more "mellow" person than he was before his stroke. Among his current great pleasures is bird watching, an activity he enjoys while continuing his musical endeavors. "Edwin walks with a cane, and he says he's much more male than he ever was. And one of the things that gives him great pleasure is bird watching, and he continues to release records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Miraculous Recovery Aided by Wife
xref.body: Despite a poor prognosis, Edwin made a remarkable recovery, largely attributed to the unwavering support of his wife, Grace Maxwell. She developed a recovery method involving drawing and writing in notebooks, tasks Edwin had to perform left-handed because the strokes had rendered his right hand useless. "Prognosis was poor, but he pulled through largely because of the incredible support he got from his wife."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musical Comeback (After 4 Years)
xref.body: It took four long years for Edwin Collins to slowly return to music. Although his right hand was impaired, preventing him from strumming a guitar, he could still form chords, and he eventually resumed recording, releasing a couple of new albums. "Slowly he was able to get back into music. It took four long years. He couldn't strum his guitar anymore because of that bum right hand, but he can still form chords."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Prominence in New Pop
xref.body: Culture Club, fronted by Boy George, was a prime example of a New Pop band. Their unique visual presentation, amplified by music videos, helped them become cultural phenomena in the early 1980s. "Think Boy George and Culture Club, ABC in their Sharp Tuxedos, Orange Juice, a band of Scotland featuring Edwin Collins, Asda Camer was another, Heaven 17 was still another."

xref.title: Recovery with Wife's Support
xref.body: Despite a poor prognosis, Edwin recovered with the unwavering support of his wife, Grace Maxwell, who encouraged him to draw and write in notebooks with his left hand, as his right hand was rendered useless by the strokes. "His wife, and this was as close to a saint as you'll find, was there every step of the way. It was her idea to help his recovery by getting Edwin to draw."

xref.body: Edwin Borsheim, also known as Kettle Cadaver, had a history of extreme and disturbing live performances. xref.title: Speech vs. Singing Anomaly
xref.body: Following his strokes, Edwin experienced significant stuttering when speaking. However, remarkably, when he sang, his stutter completely disappeared. "He still has trouble speaking, Edwin stutters a lot. But when he starts to sing, there's not a stutter to be heard."

xref.title: Tre Cool Joins and is Renamed
xref.body: John Cliffmeyer's departure led to the recruitment of Frank Edwin Wright III, who was teaching John drums and frequented the 924 Gilman Street punk club. Frank had previously been in a band with Lawrence Livermore, the founder of Lookout Records, who also bestowed upon him the stage name "Tre Cool." "Lawrence is also notable for being the guy who renamed Frank Edwin Wright III, Tray Cool."
